traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Phalaris arundinacea: culms 60 cm to 1.5 m tall.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Phalaris arundinacea: panicle 7 cm to 16 cm long.

appearance.organs.panicle.note: The panicle's layout, the model's choice after FNA (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page was not read): elongate and dense, its branches to 5 cm, appressed but spreading at flowering. Drawn as 30 short branches in threes, spreading as in flower, each with about 16 spikelets; the two tiny sterile florets are left out. Colours by eye: pinkish straw.

traits.note: FNA's account of the species (Barkworth, volume 24), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): panicles 5 to 40 cm long and 1 to 4 cm wide, elongate, often dense, always branched at least near the base, the branches to 5 cm, normally appressed but spreading at flowering, the spikelets single; spikelets of 3 florets, only the top one fertile, the two below it sterile, 1.5 to 2 mm; glumes nearly equal, 4 to 8.1 mm.

traits.spikelet_length_m.note: VicFlora's account of the species, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): spikelets crowded, 4 to 6 mm; glumes nearly equal, keeled; sterile lemmas 1 to 1.5 mm; fertile lemma broadly lanceolate, 2.5 to 4 mm.

traits.lemma_length_m.note: VicFlora's account of the species, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): the fertile lemma broadly lanceolate, 2.5 to 4 mm.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an invasive, tall, leafy grass that forms dense stands of reed-like stems with broad, flat blades and compact panicles that spread open in flower. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.7 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green blades; purplish then straw panicles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.life_span.note: Hitchcock (p. 534-535, no. 9): perennial, with creeping rhizomes.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Hitchcock (p. 534-535, no. 9): perennial with creeping rhizomes, a lowland hay grass of marshes and river banks (Abrams 1923, no. 3, the same).

traits.clonal.note: Hitchcock (p. 534-535, no. 9): spreads by creeping rhizomes.

traits.lower_glume_length_m.note: Hitchcock (p. 535, no. 9): glumes about 5 mm long, narrow, acute, the keel very narrowly winged; the genus has the glumes equal. Abrams 1923 (no. 3) gives 4 mm.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): leaf-blades 10-20 cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): leaf-blades 5-15 mm wide.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 1 (Phalaris no. 3, fig. 254): flowers June-September in swamps and moist places.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's reed canarygrass review (Waggy 2010, read 2026-10-16): "In the Pacific Northwest, reed canarygrass seed matures in late July and early August"; read as July and August.
